answer: To resist Sybil attacks in agent economies, require each agent to provide ongoing proof-of-unique-physical-presence via dedicated sensors. An agent could track a sparrow feeding at a tidal inlet with an ivory-hued optical sensor, submitting signed, time-varying data that matches peer-observed real-world events. Fake agents cannot replicate unique sensor streams without owning the hardware, making mass identity creation costly and detectable through consensus on environmental uniqueness.
